blocks.h2: Why Pipes Freeze in Mokena Homes
blocks.intro: Mokena winters bring long stretches below freezing, and a few spots freeze first.

items.body: A hose left connected traps water in the line. It freezes, splits and leaks inside the wall when you turn it on in spring.
Lines that run along an unheated garage are exposed in a cold snap.
Plumbing in rooms over the garage can freeze when the floor below is cold.

blocks.h2: Where Pipes Freeze in Newer Mokena Homes
blocks.body: Newer homes freeze in different places than older ones. Pipes in attached garage walls, bonus rooms over garages and plumbing near rim joists in the basement are common trouble spots. A hose left connected to an outdoor faucet can split the pipe inside the wall. A little insulation and a few habits prevent most of it.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: How do I keep my outdoor spigot from freezing?
items.preview: Disconnect the hose and shut off the inside valve.
items.answer: Disconnect the hose in the fall, close the shutoff inside and open the spigot to drain it. A frost-proof spigot makes it easier.

items.q: What should I do if a pipe is frozen but not burst?
items.preview: Open the faucet and warm the pipe gently.
items.answer: Open the faucet and warm the pipe gently with a hair dryer. Never use an open flame. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: Can you repair a burst pipe in a finished wall?
items.answer: Yes. We open only what we need to reach the break and fix it.
Often, for sudden damage. Policies vary, so check with your agent.

items.q: Can a burst pipe happen in a newer home?
items.answer: Yes. Pipes in garages, attics and outside walls can freeze in any home.
